ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of shareholders, directors, and UBOs against the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, Canada's Criminal Code, Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (JVCFOA). Enhanced due diligence required for Politically Exposed Persons, defined under FINTRAC guidance, including family members and close associates, with ongoing transaction monitoring and record-keeping for at least 5 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Registre des entreprises (https://registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French-language name is mandatory under the Charter of the French Language (Bill 101); English may be used only in conjunction with a French denomination; Latin-script transliteration required; registered trademarks are exempt from translation under s. 66 of the Charter.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: One renewal of up to 90 days may be requested before expiry. Upon rejection by the Registraire des entreprises, the applicant may file a written review request under s. 26 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises within 30 days of rejection. If upheld, appeal may be made to the Superior Court of Quebec under the Code of Civil Procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as sole registered address. Quebec requires a physical head office address within Quebec where legal notices and service of process may be delivered. Managed office suites are acceptable only if they provide a dedicated physical street address and a written service-of-process acceptance agreement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – estimated 5% annual probability for low-risk enterprise SaaS activities; FINTRAC and Quebec registry authorities may conduct periodic unannounced compliance visits, but risk is minimal for this industry.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c. S-31.1, including provisions governing incorporation, articles, registered office, share capital, directors, officers, corporate records, and beneficial ownership disclosures, particularly sections 4, 5, 21-32, 105-111, and 118-121, subject to the current consolidated text.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Register), administered by the Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for constitution of a Québec business corporation and accompanying articles of constitution filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, generally submitted through the online enterprise registration service.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum issued or paid-up capital applies. Shares may be issued for consideration permitted by the Business Corporations Act (Québec), including cash, property, or services where legally acceptable. Québec law does not require a capital escrow account for incorporation. The corporation must maintain accurate share subscription, issuance, and securities-register records.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the corporation accept and record the subscription by the incorporator for the number and class of shares specified in the subscription agreement, for the stated consideration, and issue those shares as fully paid when the consideration is received. RESOLVED that the registered office be established at [Québec address] and that the corporate records be maintained there or at another legally permitted location. RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to serve until replacement or resignation. The officers are authorized to execute incorporation, banking, tax, employment, and commercial documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate form, name, and Québec eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online enterprise registration service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a Québec business corporation. Conduct a corporate-name search and, where using a non-number name, assess distinctiveness, prohibited terms, French-language requirements, and potential trademark conflicts. A numbered corporation may be used if name clearance is not required. Confirm a registered office in Québec and identify the incorporator, directors, officers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficiaries.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or requested numbered-company designation
Director, officer, shareholder, and ultimate-beneficiary information
Business description: enterprise cloud software applications development and B2B SaaS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace or amend the proposed name, provide additional French-language or identity information, and resubmit through the registry portal. A refused name decision should be reviewed against the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and applicable administrative-review procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Québec Enterprise Register filing portal and, where applicable, a Québec notary or lawyer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the application for constitution, articles, share provisions, registered-office details, director information, and initial beneficial-ownership disclosures. Execute documents in accordance with the corporation's signing authority. Notarization is generally not required for the registry filing, but certified copies, powers of attorney, or foreign corporate documents should be notarized or legalized when requested by the registry, financial institution, or professional advisor.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
Certified or legalized foreign corporate documents, if an incorporator or shareholder is a foreign entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to registry deficiencies within the stated period, correct incomplete fields or attachments, and pay any additional processing fee. Retain the original signed documents and proof of submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit filing and obtain Québec enterprise number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the constitution application electronically, pay the applicable Québec fee in Canadian dollars, and monitor the portal for acceptance or queries. Upon acceptance, download the certificate or confirmation of constitution, Québec enterprise number (NEQ), filed articles, and registry extract. The corporation should not represent that it is incorporated until acceptance is issued.
required_dossiers: Government-issued identification or corporate authorization, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected fields or documents and resubmit. For a disputed refusal, request written reasons and pursue the available administrative review or judicial review route. Preserve filing receipts and the original rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's registered office, board of directors, and Québec Enterprise Register where amendments are reportable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or sign written resolutions. Adopt the registered office, appoint officers, approve the share subscription and issuance, authorize banking, approve accounting and tax representatives, adopt signing authorities, and establish the corporate records book. Record share certificates or uncertificated securities, subscription consideration, directors' consents, and conflicts-of-interest procedures.
required_dossiers: Share issuance register and securities register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Ratify defective acts by a properly authorized board or shareholder resolution, correct the corporate records, and file any required amendment or update with the registry. Obtain legal advice before curing an invalid issuance or director appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax, payroll, and operational accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Revenu Québec, and Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain or confirm the CRA business number and applicable corporate income-tax, GST/HST, payroll, and import-export accounts. Register for Québec corporate income tax, Québec sales tax (QST), source deductions, and employer accounts where thresholds or activities require registration. Assess the place-of-supply treatment of SaaS, non-resident customer sales, marketplace collections, and cross-border withholding obligations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to CRA or Revenu Québec verification requests with incorporation, ownership, banking, and business-activity evidence. Correct registration effective dates and file late returns or elections where necessary, including applicable interest and penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish privacy, cybersecurity, and commercial compliance controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec, Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, and applicable municipal authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For SaaS operations, implement Québec private-sector privacy governance under the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, including a privacy officer, privacy policy, incident-response process, data-retention controls, vendor contracts, and cross-border data-transfer assessments. Assess federal PIPEDA application and customer contractual security requirements. Obtain any municipal occupancy or signage approvals for physical premises.
required_dossiers: Municipal occupancy or signage documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remediate identified privacy or municipal deficiencies, document corrective actions, and respond to regulator inquiries. Report qualifying privacy incidents and maintain evidence of consent, safeguards, contractual controls, and breach assessments.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ordinary B2B SaaS development and cloud-software operations. If a physical industrial facility, server installation, construction project, or regulated activity is added, the relevant Québec authority may include the Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs, the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie, and the applicable municipality.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific manufacturing or industrial operating licence is ordinarily required for enterprise cloud software applications development or B2B SaaS. Municipal occupancy, zoning, construction, signage, and business-permit requirements may apply to physical premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt or not applicable for office-based SaaS development with no industrial process, material processing, significant emissions, wastewater discharge, or hazardous-waste generation. A project-specific review is required if the business constructs or operates a data centre, backup power installation, industrial plant, or other designated project.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine SaaS-specific discharge or emissions threshold applies to ordinary office operations. Any wastewater, air emissions, fuel storage, refrigerants, hazardous materials, construction runoff, or waste streams must comply with applicable Québec environmental approvals, municipal sewer requirements, hazardous-waste rules, and federal requirements. Data-centre projects may require permits for generators, cooling systems, water use, noise, and atmospheric emissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No special industrial clearance is ordinarily required for a standard SaaS office. The premises must satisfy municipal building, occupancy, zoning, accessibility, and fire-code requirements, including fire-alarm, emergency-exit, evacuation, and occupant-load rules. Structural-load certification is required where equipment, racks, generators, or construction changes affect building loads. Workplace health and safety obligations, preventive programs, training, incident reporting, and worker compensation registration are administered principally through the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal for obtaining a Business Number (BN) and program accounts. Revenu Quebec administers Quebec corporate income tax and, generally, Quebec sales tax (QST), through its online services and clicSÉQUR platform. A Quebec corporation also generally requires registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ), which is a corporate registry identifier rather than a tax identification number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign corporation conducting business in Canada should obtain a CRA Business Number through Business Registration Online or the applicable non-resident registration process, provide legal formation documents, registered address, directors, ownership information, business activities, authorized representative details, and the effective date of Canadian activities, and open the required program accounts, including GST/HST, payroll, import-export, and corporation income tax accounts as applicable. A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Quebec should separately assess Quebec corporate income tax, QST, and Quebec employer registration obligations. GST/HST registration is generally required when taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold, subject to special rules for non-resident digital-economy suppliers and voluntary registration. QST registration may be required under Quebec's specified-system rules, including separate rules for non-resident suppliers and specified digital economy supplies. Registration applications may require a Canadian representative, security, supporting documents, and proof of commercial activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no general United States-style check-the-box election for corporations. A corporation incorporated in Canada is generally a separate taxpayer subject to federal corporate income tax and, where applicable, Quebec corporate income tax. Relevant statutory elections concern transactions and tax attributes rather than elective entity classification, including section 85 rollovers for eligible property transfers, section 86 reorganizations, section 97(2) partnership transfers, amalgamations, wind-ups, and designated surplus or foreign-affiliate elections. Canadian hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions or impose income inclusions for specified deduction or inclusion mismatches; they do not provide a general elective pass-through classification. A foreign entity's Canadian classification is determined under Canadian law based on its legal characteristics and applicable treaty principles.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST), supplemented in Quebec by the Quebec Sales Tax (QST). Quebec generally applies 5.0% GST and 9.975% QST, producing a combined headline consumption-tax rate of 14.975% on fully taxable Quebec supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, measured under the GST/HST small-supplier rules, generally triggers mandatory GST/HST registration. Quebec's QST has separate registration rules and thresholds, including special rules for non-resident suppliers of specified digital economy supplies; the applicable threshold depends on the supplier's residence, registration status, customer type, and supply classification. A supplier may register voluntarily before exceeding the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not generally require real-time government clearance, continuous transaction controls, or mandatory electronic fiscal stamping for ordinary B2B SaaS invoices. Electronic invoices are generally acceptable if they preserve invoice integrity, accessibility, and required tax information. GST/HST invoices must contain prescribed information, including supplier identity and GST/HST registration number, date, recipient information where applicable, description, consideration, tax rate, and tax amount. QST invoices must satisfy Quebec documentation requirements where QST is charged. CRA and Revenu Quebec may require electronic filing of returns and records through their portals, and electronic records must be retained in an auditable form, generally for at least six years after the end of the relevant period unless a different statutory period applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of qualifying goods may be zero-rated for GST/HST when the goods are exported from Canada under the statutory export conditions and the supplier retains evidence of export. Certain supplies of services to non-residents may be zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident and the statutory conditions are satisfied. For B2B SaaS, the result depends on the legal characterization of the supply, customer status and location, place-of-supply rules, and exclusions. A service is not automatically zero-rated merely because the customer pays from outside Canada. The supplier should verify that the customer is a non-resident, obtain satisfactory non-residency evidence, document contractual service delivery and user locations, and confirm that no exclusion applies, including services in relation to Canadian real property, tangible personal property, or services performed in Canada where the relevant zero-rating provision does not apply. Input tax credits or rebates generally require valid supporting documentation and commercial-use evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Border Services Agency export declaration or applicable export reporting record for goods where export reporting is required
Commercial invoice, purchase order, customer contract, and packing list identifying the goods, supplier, purchaser, destination, value, and terms of sale
Bill of lading, air waybill, courier record, or other carrier evidence showing export from Canada
Proof of delivery or foreign importation, where available

For zero-rated services, executed customer agreement, customer non-residency evidence, billing records, service-delivery and user-location records, and evidence supporting the applicable GST/HST zero-rating provision

Foreign-exchange and payment records, including bank statements or payment processor records, where relevant to commercial substantiation; Canada does not generally require an inward remittance certificate for GST/HST zero-rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory requirement to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days and no general foreign-exchange surrender rule. CRA or Revenu Quebec may deny zero-rating, input tax credits, rebates, or refunds where export, non-residency, place-of-supply, or documentary requirements are not proven, and reassess tax retroactively with applicable interest. GST/HST penalties may apply for false statements, omissions, late filing, failure to remit, or unsupported input tax credits; gross-negligence penalties can generally equal 50% of the understated tax or improperly claimed amount. Quebec may impose corresponding QST assessments, interest, and penalties. Failure to maintain records or produce supporting evidence may result in adverse assessments. Improper customs declarations may trigger Canada Border Services Agency Administrative Monetary Penalty System sanctions, seizure, duties and taxes, reassessment, and, in serious cases, prosecution. Intentional tax evasion, fraud, or false documentation may result in criminal fines and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) exercises monetary authority; Canada does not operate a single centralized foreign exchange control administration. The prudential regulator for federally chartered banks is the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), and the financial-intelligence unit responsible for AML/CFT supervision is the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII member and maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. The Canadian dollar floats freely and there is no central-bank permit required for inbound equity, outbound dividends, or profit repatriation. The only practical remittance hurdle is tax compliance: Canadian-resident payers must withhold Part XIII non-resident tax on dividends, interest, and royalties, generally 25% statutory but often reduced under tax treaties to 5% to 15%, with reporting through CRA Form NR4 and the Quebec revenue system where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender rules, no statutory conversion ratio, and no mandatory receipt-holding timeline. Exporters may retain foreign-currency proceeds in Canadian commercial accounts or convert to Canadian dollars at market rates. Reporting is AML-driven: financial institutions must report incoming and outgoing electronic transfers of C$10,000 or more to FINTRAC, and physical cross-border movements of currency of C$10,000 or more must be declared to the Canada Border Services Agency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account in CAD/USD and RBC USD Premium Account for cross-border treasury
Canadian-dollar Business Operating Account with USD clearing via the TD Bank US network
Operating Account and BMO U.S. Dollar Business Account with cross-border cash management
Operating Account / CIBC U.S. Dollar Account and commercial letter-of-credit services
International Business Account / Operating Account with North American and Latin American USD clearing
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account with strong Quebec commercial presence and AMF-related trust services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is medium for payment facilitation but low as a sole treasury bank. Offshore digital EMIs cannot directly connect to Payments Canada Lynx clearing or operate as the primary CAD settlement bank unless they are authorized or registered as a money services business under PCMLTFA and, where operating in Quebec, comply with Quebec money-services regulation under the Autorité des marchés financiers. Wise Business/B2B is operationally viable for supplier payouts, payroll in foreign currencies, and small disbursements, but it should be used only as a non-bank payout rail; primary liquidity, FX, and commercial banking must remain with a Canadian Schedule I bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a low-risk Quebec-resident B2B SaaS corporation with no regulated activity, directors may generally complete remote digital KYC if the ultimate beneficial owner has Canadian identity documentation, the Quebec registraire des entreprises record is clear, and the corporate contract pack is complete. However, for a non-resident parent entity with 25% or more ownership, or where signatories have no Canadian identity, Canadian banks commonly require an in-person branch interview or a notarized/video-verified identity session, board resolutions, certificate of corporate existence, source-of-funds evidence, and group organizational charts before any inbound capital is credited or released.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated Quebec subsidiary with a non-resident ultimate beneficial owner, no local operating history, and no bank relationship; the bank risk committee flags shell-company risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certificate and articles of incorporation, Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), complete UBO register, audited or reviewed financial statements, executed B2B SaaS customer contracts, board resolution appointing signatories, source-of-funds statement from the parent, and a group holding-structure chart with jurisdiction of residency for each owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital contribution from a related offshore holding company without a documented equity or intercompany loan agreement; account opening unit suspects undisclosed financing or layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver an executed share-subscription agreement or shareholders resolution, intercompany loan agreement at arm's-length rates, paid-up capital ledger, treasury management plan, audited parent financials, group tax identification numbers, confirmation of Canadian foreign-reporting filings (Form T1134/T1135 if applicable), and an undertaking to disclose any material UBO change in Quebec corporate registers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound supplier payments to a jurisdiction that is not a FATF member or that is perceived as a dual-use software hub; sanctions screening flags jurisdiction risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide end-client agreements, invoice trail, full settlement terms, export-control and end-use declarations, Canadian denied-party screening results, technology classification memo demonstrating that the SaaS software is generic commercial software outside the Export Control List, supplier KYC pack, and confirmation of compliance with the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent subscription receipts from multiple start-up counterparties creating repeated electronic funds transfers at or above C$10,000 and automated EFT reporting clusters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a customer KYC pack with confirmation that all counterparties are identifiable legal persons, a risk-based AML/ATF policy, FINTRAC reporting procedure, payment-rail reconciliation, contract database, and evidence of recurring SaaS subscription billing rather than pass-through or store-and-forward transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a SWIFT MT103 from the parent or related investor to the Canadian entity's Schedule I bank account with a clear payment narrative stating equity subscription under corporate law and the Canadian business number / registraire des entreprises identifier. Canada has no statutory FX-purpose code regime, so Canadian banks rely on the wire narrative and supporting corporate documents; if the remittance is C$10,000 or more, FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting applies automatically. If the foreign parent is establishing a new Canadian business, an Investment Canada Act notification may be mandatory for non-cultural B2B SaaS operations, although standard enterprise values remain below review thresholds; update Quebec registraire des entreprises records to match the subscription and avoid UBO mismatches.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settle supplier invoices through Payments Canada Lynx real-time gross settlement wires (SWIFT MT103) for same-day CAD obligations, through irrevocable commercial letters of credit for large cross-border procurement, and through Wise B2B or local payout rails for smaller disbursements where beneficiary account details are known. For each outbound wire include beneficiary legal name, full bank identifier, invoice number, and a clear payment narrative to reduce sanctions and reconciliation exceptions. USD clearing generally routes through the Canadian bank's U.S. correspondent or a U.S. agency, requiring OFAC screening in addition to Canadian sanctions screening; maintain OFAC, UN, and Special Economic Measures Act screening for all payees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/GBP FX forwards under ISDA/CSA with a Canadian Schedule I bank
Flexible or vanilla FX forwards for forecast B2B SaaS subscription, payroll, and vendor-payable cash flows
FX swaps and rollovers used to manage short-term cross-currency liquidity between operating accounts and intercompany loans
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for intercompany capital structures, subject to board authorization and an OSFI-regulated counterparty
Plain-vanilla bought FX options for discrete transaction exposures confirmed by monthly treasury forecasting

Non-deliverable forwards or NDFs only for emerging-market currencies that are not deliverable in Canada; no NDF is required or normally permissible for CAD pairs because the Canadian dollar is fully convertible onshore

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties up to $500 CAD, potential administrative dissolution if not remedied

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the corporation has 10 or more shareholders and qualifies as a distributing corporation
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of directors and officers; beneficial ownership register updates required upon shareholding transfers

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general active-business rate (15% federal General Rate Reduction + 11.5% Quebec); CCPC small-business rate 14% on first CAD 500,000 active-business income (9% federal + 5% Quebec)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction for CCPCs; federal SR&ED refundable investment tax credit of up to 35% on qualifying R&D expenditures (small CCPC); Quebec R&D tax credits; Quebec patent-box deduction for eligible IP income; accelerated CCA on Class 50 computer hardware and Class 12 software; other sector-specific innovation credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return — filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via EFILE/Netfile; T2 paper filing available to mandated filers
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be filed within six (6) months of the corporation's fiscal period end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number (BN), province of operation, mailing address, fiscal year-end, and director/officer information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation with a permanent establishment in Canada, set out the PE address, PE branch name, and the Canadian agent/representative's contact data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record gross enterprise SaaS license and subscription revenue, implementation/professional services revenue, and any incidental revenue streams.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue attributable to the Canadian PE; cloud-based SaaS revenue may require allocation under OECD PE attribution rules if the service is rendered through a PE in the province.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim trade, marketing, infrastructure, R&D and SR&ED expenditures; compute cross-border cost allocations, depreciation, and amortization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure deductions relate to income earned from Canadian-source activities; transfer-priced cross-border charges must align with arm's length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile financial net income to taxable income and compute federal tax, including the general rate reduction and provincial abatement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taxable income for the PE is determined under the same charging provisions; only the PE's Canadian-source ABI is subject to federal Part I tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply non-capital loss carryforwards (up to 20 years) against certain source income; capital loss offsets limited to capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations may claim carryforwards only to the extent losses are attributable to the Canadian PE and remain within the PE's source computation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: CRA late-filing penalty: 5% of unpaid balance + 1% per month (max 12 months) for T2; gross negligence could add up to 50% of unreported tax or a 10% transfer-pricing adjustment penalty; criminal tax evasion can add fines up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment.
